# Changelog

## Unreleased

### Features

- [go-stricttest] **An ephemeral PostgreSQL cluster for Go suites.** `pgcluster.Start` and `Stop` boot a throwaway postmaster on a private unix socket for a `TestMain`, `Ephemeral(t, ...)` scopes one to a single test, and `Database(t)` hands each test its own database under the DSN environment variable you name. Zero dependencies: `initdb`, `pg_ctl` and `psql` are driven as subprocesses, never a linked driver.

## 0.1.1

Fix the CI router paths filter so a batch release's tagged commit runs every project's test suite

<details>
<summary>Context</summary>

The 0.1.0 batch release landed every releasable's tag on the final "snapshot"
commit, which touches only .rlsbl-monorepo/snapshot.json. No project's paths
filter matched that file, so the CI router reported
"go-stricttest-ci / test: skipped" on the tagged commit and the publish gate
refused to treat a skipped check as passing.

The fix adds .rlsbl-monorepo/snapshot.json and
.rlsbl-monorepo/releasables/<name>/** to every project's watch patterns, so the
commit a batch release actually tags now triggers all three suites. This release
runs the corrected pipeline end to end and resyncs all three releasables to
0.1.1.

</details>

### Infrastructure

- Fix the CI router paths filter so a batch release's tagged commit runs every project's test suite

## 0.1.0

### Features

- [go-stricttest] **New: the `hygiene` package.** One `hygiene.Isolate(t)` call gives a Go test a throwaway `HOME`, an empty git config with a throwaway identity, `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file`, and an environment stripped of every ambient credential -- all restored when the test ends. Granular helpers (`ThrowawayHome`, `IsolateGitConfig`, `LockdownTransports`, `StripCredentials`, `Chdir`) and a closed `Preserve` enum for toolchain caches ship alongside it.
- [go-stricttest] **`ThrowawayHome` and `LockdownTransports` now cover more ground.** `ThrowawayHome` repoints `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME` and `XDG_STATE_HOME` into the throwaway home as well as `HOME`, so a tool that reads the XDG dirs first (gh, for one) can no longer see the developer's real config or write into their real caches. `LockdownTransports` additionally pins `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` and `GIT_PROXY_COMMAND` to `/bin/false`, so lifting `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL` no longer hands git the developer's real ssh key. This brings the Go module to parity with the Python floor.
